title: PDF Passwords and Permissions: What They Do and Don't Do
description: A plain-language guide to PDF open passwords, permissions, limitations and safe handling before sending a protected document.
intro: PDF security settings can restrict opening or discourage certain actions in compatible readers. They are useful controls, but they do not prevent every kind of copying or disclosure. Understand the goal and test the protected file before sharing it.

sections.heading: Open passwords and permissions are different
paragraphs: An open password asks for a credential before the document can be viewed. Permissions settings may signal or restrict actions such as printing or editing in readers that honor those settings.
Reader support varies. Permissions are not a substitute for controlling who receives the file, and they cannot prevent screenshots, photography or every method of reproducing visible information.

sections.heading: Use sensible password handling
paragraphs: Follow your organization's policy and use a unique password appropriate to the sensitivity of the document. Do not put the password in the same message as the protected file if a separate channel is available.
Keep a secure record if the document must remain accessible later. Losing the password can make recovery difficult or impossible, depending on the PDF and encryption used.

sections.heading: Protect a copy and test it
paragraphs: Use Protect PDF to create a protected copy. Open the result in a compatible reader, verify that the password prompt appears as intended and confirm that authorized recipients can access it.
If the goal is to conceal information, password protection alone is not redaction. Use Redact PDF for content that must be removed, and inspect metadata separately when needed.

faq.question: Does a PDF permission setting stop people from taking screenshots?
faq.answer: No. Permissions may be honored by compatible readers but cannot prevent screenshots, photography or every way of reproducing visible content.

faq.question: Should I send the password in the same email as the PDF?
faq.answer: For sensitive files, follow your organization's policy and consider sharing credentials through a separate approved channel.

faq.question: Does password protection hide metadata?
faq.answer: Not necessarily. Password protection and metadata removal are separate operations; inspect document properties if they matter.

faq.question: Can I use a password instead of redaction?
faq.answer: No. If content should not be disclosed even to recipients who can open the file, remove it with a true redaction workflow and verify the output.
